Today's AI briefing from The Gradient | 2026-11-27

1. Constraint-Aware Test-Time Scoring for LLM and VLM Candidate Selection
A team proposes a constraint‑aware scoring framework for large language (LLM) and vision‑language models (VLM) that evaluates multiple candidate answers at inference time. The method layers a small set of immutable checks (e.g., physical feasibility, domain‑specific rules) on top of traditional confidence or…

2. Dynamic Reasoning in Next-Gen Detection and Response: An Empirical Study of LLM Triage, Reinforcement Tuning, and Adversarial Evasion
Researchers ran 56 reproducible experiments across a multi‑layer enterprise‑cloud simulator and four public datasets (SOREL‑20M, BODMAS, LANL, DARPA) to compare static classifiers, graph‑based signal fusion, and LLM triage agents when analysts have strict attention budgets (Recall at B alerts/day).

3. FIG-MAC: A Fine-grained Inspiration Graph Empowered Multi-Agent Collaboration for Automated Scientific Hypothesis Generation
Researchers released FIG-MAC, a system that builds an inspiration graph linking concepts at a granular level and deploys multiple LLM agents to explore, combine, and refine these links into concrete, verifiable hypotheses.
